Q: How do you set a strftime with javascript? A:

In addition to Walter Chapilliquen - wZVanG's correct answer, I would suggest use of navigator.language:

const dateOpt = {
        weekday: 'short',
        month: 'short',
        day: 'numeric',
        year: 'numeric',
        hour: 'numeric',
        minute: 'numeric',
        second: 'numeric'
};
console.log(
    new Date().toLocaleString(
        [ navigator.language, 'en'],
        dateOpt
    )
);

Q: How to import and manipulate a CSV dataset in R? A:

read.csv is the beginner's best way to read a csv file. If your data comes from a place/country where the decimal point is comma, use read.csv2 instead. As for how to access rows and columns, please take a look at An Introduction to R, file R-intro.pdf, that comes with all installations of R. Read at least up to chapter 6.

Q: How to count how many consecutive days I had over an specific temperature? (in R) A:

Here are some ideas in parts based on 1, 2.

with the data

X <- data.frame(Year = rep(1992L, 9), Month = rep(1L, 9), Day = 13L:21L, Temperature = c(20.68, 20.82, 21.66, 22.04, 23.32, 23.91, 23.54, 21.89, 21.95),p90 = c(21.95, 21.95, 21.95, 21.95, 21.95, 21.95, 21.95, 21.95, 21.95), cd_expected = c(0L, 0L, 0L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 0L, 0L))

{base} R

Using run length encoding rle we capture the lengths of each condition and sequence along it, then multiply with the condition which is 0 if not met.

cond <- X$Temperature > X$p90
X$cd_cor_base <- sequence(rle(cond)$lengths) * cond

{data.table}

Pretty much the same idea: Count out each sequence of the group rleid(Temperature > p90) and multiply with the condition.

library(data.table)
X_dt <- setDT(copy(X))
X_dt[, cd_cor_dt := seq_len(.N) * (Temperature > p90), by = rleid(Temperature > p90)]

{collapse}

Count out conditions and group by the inverse of it using g = .

library(collapse)
cond <- X$Temperature > X$p90
X$cd_cor_col <- fcumsum(x = cond, g = fcumsum(!cond))

Benchmark

library(bench)
library(data.table)
library(collapse)

n <- 10000  
X <- data.frame(
  Temperature = c(20.68, 20.82, 21.66, 22.04, 23.32, 23.91, 23.54, 21.89, 21.95),
  p90         = 21.95
)
X      <- X[rep(seq_len(nrow(X)), n), ]
X_dt   <- as.data.table(X)
cond   <- X$Temperature > X$p90

bench::mark(
  cd_base        = sequence(rle(cond)$lengths) * cond,
  cd_dt          = X_dt[, seq_len(.N) * (Temperature > p90), by = rleid(Temperature > p90)]$V1,
  cd_collapse    = fcumsum(cond, fcumsum(!cond)),
  min_iterations = 100
)

Q: How to define document in JavaScript A:

A quick way to remove all the JS Lint markers for "document is not defined" is to put "var document;" at the top of your JS file, just so you can see more clearly what the real errors are.

Do not leave "var document;" within the JS file though as it can cause problems.

Q: How do I restore a supabase db from a .backup file? A:

A .backup file from Supabase is a PostgreSQL custom-format dump (created via pg_dump -Fc). You can restore it using pg_restore against your new project's connection string.

In your new Supabase dashboard, go to Project Settings → Database and copy the connection string. It'll look like:

postgresql://postgres:[YOUR-PASSWORD]@db.[YOUR-PROJECT-REF].supabase.co:5432/postgres

Then, restore using pg_restore

bash

pg_restore \
  --clean \
  --if-exists \
  --no-owner \
  --no-privileges \
  -d "postgresql://postgres:[YOUR-PASSWORD]@db.[YOUR-PROJECT-REF].supabase.co:5432/postgres" \
  your_file.backup
